newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan stocks down, but response to rate hike mute.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan stocks down, but response to rate hike mute.

text.p: Taiwan share prices remained mildly lower in late trade on Friday, showing a relatively mute response to the central bank's decision to hike two key interest rates, brokers said.
* At 0106 GMT, index down 0.37 percent or 36.97 points at 10,029.38, but recovered from intra-day low of 9,953.31.

* Central bank on Thursday announced modest tightening of monetary policy by raising rediscount rate to 5.25 percent from 5.00 and accommodations against secured loans to 5.625 percent from 5.375, effective from Friday.

* Amy Huang, analyst, Nomura Securities: "Raising the two rates serves more symbolic than real purposes. They are the rates the central bank tampers with in order to make a point, rather than to launch actual policy changes."
* Constructions fall 1.27 percent and financials 0.91 percent on jitters over slightly higher capital requirements for investments after the rate hikes, brokers say.
* Recent rally bellwether electronics rise 0.16 percent, buoyed by expectations of surging late 1997 sales orders.
